design.title: RequirementPilot: Independent Project Analysis — Committee Defense Briefing

design.reference: Formal university committee briefing; matches the deep-teal DM-1 design of the companion Word report

slides.title: Cover
slides.task_brief: Cover slide, left-aligned hero composition on --bg with a deep teal (--primary-deep to --primary) vertical panel or band on the left third for contrast (white text on it). Eyebrow: 'INDEPENDENT PROJECT ANALYSIS · COMMITTEE BRIEFING'. Main title (font-heading, --fs-display): 'RequirementPilot'. Subtitle (2 lines, --fs-h3, muted): 'An evidence-grounded, human-in-the-loop, agentic requirements engineering platform — deep analysis of the reference document dated 30 September 2026.' Prominent verdict chip (accent --accent bg soft, white or accent text): 'CONDITIONAL GO · CONSOLIDATED SCORE 4.0 / 5'. Meta row at bottom (fs-small, muted): 'Analysis briefing · October 2026' + 'Prepared for the supervisor and defense committee' + 'Companion to the 27-page written analysis report (11 sections · 5 figures · 10 tables)'. Use the .rule-accent bar above the title. No images.

slides.title: Briefing roadmap
slides.task_brief: Agenda slide titled 'Briefing roadmap' with .rule-accent under an eyebrow 'AGENDA'. Four horizontal rows (cards or divided list), each with a .num-badge number, bold part title, and one-line description: 01 'Verdict at a Glance' — What the platform is, and how it scores across six assessment dimensions. 02 'Novelty & Contribution' — Ten planned contributions; two defensible research cores (N2, N7), eight disciplined increments. 03 'Feasibility, Architecture & Risk' — Sound, conservative design; schedule arithmetic with zero buffer; eleven risks, four newly identified. 04 'Actions & Recommendation' — Twelve actions across three time horizons, the descope ladder, and four conditions attached to the go. Right side or background: a subtle oversized ghost numeral or vertical 'RP' watermark in --primary-soft. No images.

slides.title: Section 01 — Verdict at a Glance
slides.task_brief: Section divider. Full-bleed deep teal background (--primary-deep to --primary gradient allowed), white text. Chapter marker '01 / 04' (font-num, large, semi-transparent white). Section title (font-heading, --fs-display): 'Verdict at a Glance'. Tagline (max 2 lines, white 85% opacity): '"An exceptionally well-prepared graduation project — honest about the literature, precise about its mechanisms, disciplined about evaluation."' Bottom row of three small white-outline chips: '6 dimensions scored' · '4 conditions attached' · 'No structural flaws found'. No images.

slides.title: What is RequirementPilot?
slides.task_brief: Title: 'What is RequirementPilot?'. Lead paragraph (2–3 sentences, --fs-h3 weight normal): 'Rather than generating polished requirements from a single prompt, RequirementPilot conducts structured stakeholder interviews, distinguishes explain-why questions from extraction tasks, and grounds every requirement in versioned evidence. Humans approve each transition — no requirement gap is ever silently filled by a model.' Below, a stat band of 4 stat cards (large font-num number + small label): '10' planned contributions (N1–N10); '7' research questions with quantitative metrics; '8' recent systems benchmarked in the literature review; '3' evidence languages — English, Egyptian Arabic, code-switched. Bottom strip (card-soft, one line): 'Team of four · 6-month (24-week) graduation project window · Integration-first positioning that explicitly forbids overclaiming novelty.' No images.

slides.title: Consolidated verdict
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Consolidated verdict — conditional go at 4.0 / 5'. Left 52%: .figure-frame with image at RELATIVE path ../assets_rp/fig5_scores.png (horizontal bar chart of six dimension scores; keep aspect, do not crop). Right 48%: compact six-row list, each row = dimension name, bold score in font-num, and a micro strength/weakness pair: 'Strategic positioning 4.0 — integration-first, honestly framed / framing A–D not yet chosen'; 'Novelty & research gap 4.0 — N2 + N7 defensible cores / self-assessed matrix, no search protocol'; 'Technical architecture 4.0 — determinism-first, authority-aware retrieval / context, concurrency, observability unspecified'; 'Evaluation methodology 4.5 — strategies, not models; full ablation map / no power analysis or IAA plan'; 'Feasibility & schedule 3.0 — clear MVP and M1 gate / 26 weeks of work in 24; benchmark last'; 'Reference-document quality 5.0 — comprehensive, honest, actionable / none material'. Highlight the 3.0 row with a --warn left border and the 4.5 row with an --ok left border. Bottom full-width banner (card-accent): 'Proceed — subject to four conditions, detailed in Part 04.'

slides.title: Section 02 — Novelty & Contribution
slides.task_brief: Section divider, same deep-teal full-bleed style as slide 3 (keep visual identical grammar). Chapter marker '02 / 04'. Section title: 'Novelty & Contribution'. Tagline: 'Two defensible research cores — impact-aware question selection and an Arabic code-switching benchmark — carried by eight useful but individually incremental contributions.' Small caption under tagline: 'Assessment basis: analyst scoring of the ten contributions against recent systems (RECOVER, LENS, OntoAgent, ReqElicitGym, ProReFiCIA, AraREQ, MAAD, MedNegotiator).' No images.

slides.title: Novelty matrix
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Ten contributions positioned by impact vs. feasibility'. Left 55%: .figure-frame with image at RELATIVE path ../assets_rp/fig1_novelty_matrix.png (scatter matrix; keep aspect). Right 45%: three stacked cluster cards. Card 1 (accent left border, label 'PROTECT — core of the thesis'): 'N2 Impact-aware question selection · N7 Arabic / code-switched benchmark — individually defensible, ablation-critical, independently publishable.' Card 2 (neutral, label 'KEEP — lightweight'): 'N1 Evidence-first objects · N3 Ambiguity branching · N4 Uncertainty ledger · N5 Requirement debt score · N6 Voice preservation · N10 Rationale explanations — valuable engineering, not headline research.' Card 3 (muted/dashed border, label 'DEFER — descope candidates'): 'N8 Cross-artifact change propagation · N9 Requirements time travel — Phase B material; first cuts when time compresses.' Footnote (fs-micro, muted): 'Scores are analyst estimates on a 1–5 scale; the matrix is self-assessed by the team, hence Action 2 (systematic search protocol).'

slides.title: The defensible core
slides.task_brief: Title: 'The defensible core: N2 and N7'. Two equal side-by-side panels. LEFT panel (card with teal top border, header 'N2 — Impact-aware question selection', score chips 'impact 4.8' / 'feasibility 3.4'): bullets: 'Deterministic utility scoring decides which question the interviewer asks next — no black-box agent loop'; 'The system's central claim stands or falls with this mechanism: ablation-critical'; 'Weakness: utility weights are currently unjustified guesses → pilot ablation on the first 20 scenarios in month 3 (Action 7)'. RIGHT panel (card with terracotta top border, header 'N7 — Egyptian Arabic / code-switched benchmark', score chips 'impact 4.6' / 'feasibility 3.0'): bullets: 'First requirements benchmark of its kind for Egyptian Arabic and code-switching; independently publishable'; 'Aligned with team skills — dedicated NLP/Arabic member — and with the local context'; 'Weakness: currently scheduled in months 5–6, too late to evaluate properly → production from month 2 (Action 6)'. Bottom full-width strip (card-soft): 'Why these two are defensible: both are measurable, both have drawn boundaries (exact dialect, task, benchmark limits), and both match available skills and data.'

slides.title: Section 03 — Feasibility, Architecture & Risk
slides.task_brief: Section divider, same deep-teal full-bleed style as slides 3 and 6. Chapter marker '03 / 04'. Section title: 'Feasibility, Architecture & Risk'. Tagline: 'Sound, deliberately conservative engineering — set against schedule arithmetic with zero buffer and a risk cluster concentrated in execution, not in the idea.' Three small white-outline chips: 'Architecture 4.0 / 5' · 'Schedule 3.0 / 5' · '11 risks mapped'. No images.

slides.title: Architecture review
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Architecture: conservative by design — and right'. Left 48%: .figure-frame with image at RELATIVE path ../assets_rp/fig2_architecture.png (five-layer architecture diagram; keep aspect). Right 52%: two stacked cards. Card 'What is strong' (.tick items): 'Explicit state machine instead of a heavyweight agent framework — no hidden non-determinism in a system whose thesis is determinism'; 'Evidence is a first-class object: 22-entity model, event-style requirement versioning (never overwrite; author, source, reason, timestamp stored)'; 'Authority-aware retrieval: approved policies (authority 1.00 / 0.95) cannot be silently overridden by AI inference (0.3×)'; 'Eight hallucination controls wrapped around the human approval gate.' Card 'What is unspecified' (.cross item): 'Context management, concurrency, and observability are not yet designed → run graph-query and infrastructure spikes before Phase 3 (Action 5).'

slides.title: Evaluation methodology
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Evaluation methodology — the strongest dimension (4.5 / 5)'. Three equal columns as cards. Column 1 header '7 research questions': 'Each RQ carries named metrics — extraction accuracy (RQ1), utility of asked questions, conflict-detection quality, trace-link precision — and the design evaluates interview strategies, not model impressions.' Column 2 header 'Disciplined baselines': 'Four interview strategies — single-shot generation, unrestricted conversational LLM, ontology-guided interviewer, impact-aware planner — crossed with a four-language matrix, plus three artifact-validation baselines.' Column 3 header 'Layered data strategy': 'Public corpora first: PURE (79 documents, 34,268 sentences), PROMISE and SWARD where licensing permits; ReqElicitGym (101 scenarios) for baseline runs; real conversations only where permissions allow.' Bottom full-width gap banner (card-accent, icon 'warning'): 'Missing before any data collection: statistical power analysis, random seeds, significance testing plan, and an inter-annotator agreement threshold → fixed by Action 3 (weeks 1–2).'

slides.title: Schedule feasibility
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Schedule feasibility — the weakest dimension (3.0 / 5)'. Left 55%: .figure-frame with image at RELATIVE path ../assets_rp/fig3_gantt.png (Gantt chart with 24-week deadline line; keep aspect). Right 45% vertical rail of 4 compact point cards: '1 · Arithmetic: nine phases sum to 18–26 weeks against a 24-week window — zero buffer at maximum durations'; '2 · Composition: the two most valuable contributions are the two most expensive — planner ablations need Phase 3 stable; the Arabic benchmark sits in months 5–6'; '3 · Concentration: the question planner is a single-owner critical path (Member 1) — co-assign in month 3 (Action 8)'; '4 · Team: sensible four-way split (LLM/interview · NLP/Arabic/data · backend/graph · frontend/QA), but execution-side risk is underweighted in the document.'

slides.title: Risk register
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Risk register — 11 risks; four identified by this analysis'. Left 46%: .figure-frame with image at RELATIVE path ../assets_rp/fig4_risk_grid.png (probability–severity grid; keep aspect). Right 54%: ranked exposure list of 5 rows (each: bold ID chip, risk name, P×S score in font-num, mitigation one-liner): 'R10 Benchmark produced too late — 4.0 × 4.35 — start scenario production month 2; evaluate on the first 50 (NEW)'; 'R1 Scope explosion across 10 contributions — 4.0 × 4.0 — freeze MVP and RQ set; enforce the descope ladder (doc)'; 'R8 Annotation quality, no IAA protocol — 4.3 × 3.1 — written guidelines, double annotation on a sample, report kappa (NEW)'; 'R9 Evaluator recruitment fails in month 6 — 4.0 × 3.0 — book evaluators in month 2; pay or course credit (NEW)'; 'R7 Hallucinated requirements — 2.0 × 5.0 — evidence-first design, validation rules, human approval (doc)'. Footnote: 'Legend: teal = stated in the reference document (R1–R7); tan = identified by this analysis (R8–R11). Also watch R11 ethics/privacy (2.0 × 4.3): request Track C permissions in week 1; Track A stands alone.'

slides.title: Section 04 — Actions & Recommendation
slides.task_brief: Section divider, same deep-teal full-bleed style as slides 3, 6, 9. Chapter marker '04 / 04'. Section title: 'Actions & Recommendation'. Tagline: 'Twelve actions ordered by the deadline by which they stop being cheap — three horizons, one descope ladder, four conditions on the go decision.' Three small white-outline chips: '12 actions' · '3 horizons' · '4 conditions'. No images.

slides.title: Action plan
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Twelve actions across three horizons'. Three columns as cards with colored headers. Column 'WEEKS 1–3 — Foundations' (teal header): '1 Freeze framing (A–D), RQ wording, descope ladder' · '2 Systematic-search protocol: queries, criteria, cutoff' · '3 Annotation guidelines + statistical analysis plan (power, seeds, IAA target)' · '4 Request Track C permissions; design Track A to stand alone' · '5 Graph-query spikes against the relational schema'. Column 'MONTHS 2–3 — Momentum' (teal header): '6 Benchmark production cadence: 10 scenarios/week → 60–80 ready by month 4' · '7 Pilot utility ablation on the first 20 scenarios' · '8 Co-assign the planner; prompt versioning, logging, cost accounting' · '9 Book human evaluators (students and practitioners)'. Column 'MONTHS 5–6 — Endgame' (teal header): '10 Hold the what-not-to-build list; integrations as demo videos only' · '12 Publication: benchmark + strategy comparison as a short paper' plus an 'ONGOING' sub-block (terracotta accent): '11 Descope ladder as needed: N9 → N8 depth → N5 calibration → benchmark scale'. Bottom banner (card-accent): 'The critical three: Actions 1, 3 and 6 — freeze the contract, define the statistics, start the benchmark now.'

slides.title: Recommendation
slides.task_brief: Title: 'Recommendation: proceed — under four conditions'. Left 58%: four numbered rows (.num-badge 1–4, each bold headline + one-line detail): '1 Freeze the research contract — RQs and the minimum viable contribution locked before Phase 3'; '2 Move the benchmark left — scenario production and annotation guidelines begin in month 2, not month 5'; '3 Define the statistics first — sample sizes, seeds and IAA thresholds before any data collection'; '4 Adopt the descope ladder — change-impact and requirement-debt features are sacrificed first, by rule'. Right 42%: two stacked cards. Card 'Never descoped' (teal, icon 'lock'): 'Question planner (N2) · Evidence model · Arabic benchmark (N7)'. Card 'Descoped in order' (muted, icon 'stairs'): 'N9 Requirements time travel → N8 Change-propagation depth → N5 Debt-score calibration → Benchmark scale'. Bottom quote strip (font-heading, italic): 'These conditions are not reservations about the idea — they are the discipline the document itself prescribes, applied to its own plan.'

slides.title: Closing
slides.task_brief: Closing slide on deep teal full-bleed (mirror of section dividers), white text, centered-left composition. Large statement (font-heading, --fs-h1, max 3 lines): '"No requirement gap is ever silently filled by a model — and no plan gap silently filled by optimism."' Below, verdict line (--fs-h3, white 90%): 'Conditional go · 4.0 / 5 — held to its own standard, RequirementPilot should be accepted with distinction and leave behind a citable benchmark and a replication-ready evaluation harness.' Row of three white-outline milestone chips: 'Month 2 — 60–80 scenarios + frozen RQs' · 'Month 3 — pilot ablation results' · 'Month 6 — defense + short-paper submission'. Bottom: 'Thank you — questions welcome' with a .rule-accent bar. No images.
